about: The HTTP twin's control plane for this contract: the faults it can be told to show, and what each does to the contract's laws. The contract itself (src/) never mentions them. A law not named under a fault holds while the fault is active, for every request the model answers. Written once by `lawtwin import openapi`; yours from then on.

faults.name: latency
faults.summary: Responses are slow: each matching response is held back before it is sent.

params.name: delay
params.summary: How long, in real time, each response is held back.

params.name: jitter
params.summary: Up to this much more, drawn from the seeded generator.

params.name: operation
params.summary: Only requests for this operation; without it, every operation.

params.name: for
params.summary: How long, on the twin clock; without it, until it is cleared.

faults.changes: Only when an answer is sent. Every request reaches the model as usual.

faults.name: server-error
faults.summary: The service fails: matching requests are answered with a 5xx status and the body the document gives that status, if any.

params.name: status
params.summary: The status, 500 to 599.

params.name: operation
params.summary: Only requests for this operation of the contract, by its name; without it, every operation.

params.name: count
params.summary: How many requests it answers before it ends by itself; without it, until it is cleared.

params.name: probability
params.summary: The chance, in percent, that a matching request is affected, drawn from the seeded generator.

params.name: applied
params.summary: Whether the request reaches the model first: true runs the operation and then answers as the fault says, so the client does not learn that it took effect.

params.name: for
params.summary: How long, on the twin clock; without it, until it is cleared or used up.

faults.changes: With applied=false the request never reaches the model. With applied=true the model runs it, and the client is told it failed.

laws.a created label reads back: Holds for every read that reaches the model. A read answered with a 5xx status is not the record, so a client sees the law broken for it; a write answered with a 5xx status before it reaches the model wrote nothing, and claims nothing. With applied=true the write took effect: the record reads back once the fault lets reads through.
laws.a deleted label is not found: Holds when the delete reaches the model: with applied=true the record is gone though the client was told otherwise. A delete answered with a 5xx status before it reaches the model left the record, so a read still finds it; a read answered with a 5xx status is not NotFound.
laws.the list holds a created label: Holds for every list that reaches the model; a list answered with a 5xx status holds nothing.
laws.an update changes only the fields it giv: Holds for every update and read that reach the model; an update answered with a 5xx status before it reaches the model changed nothing, and a read answered with a 5xx status gives no record to compare.

faults.name: rate-limit
faults.summary: The service limits its rate: past `limit` requests in a window of the twin clock, requests are answered 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After, the seconds left in the window.

params.name: limit
params.summary: How many requests a window lets through; 0 refuses every one.

params.name: window
params.summary: The window, on the twin clock; it starts when the fault is raised, and the next one when it ends.

params.name: operation
params.summary: Only requests for this operation; without it, every operation, counted together.

params.name: for
params.summary: How long, on the twin clock; without it, until it is cleared.

faults.changes: A refused request never reaches the model. On the frozen clock a window ends only when a test advances the clock past it.

force.about: A forced state names records of each resource. Each is reached through the contract's own operations: a create, then an update or replace for what the create does not set; it must then read back as given. A state the operations do not reach is refused with the law that forbids it, and nothing is applied.

refusals.a created label reads back: a Label the contract's create, then its update or replace, would not read back as given: a field the service sets itself, a key the service assigns differently, a key already held, or a value that breaks the document's constraints
refusals.a created milestone reads back: a Milestone the contract's create, then its update or replace, would not read back as given: a field the service sets itself, a key the service assigns differently, a key already held, or a value that breaks the document's constraints
